simple.meaning: גְּבִירָה (gᵉbîyrâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a mistress.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: גְּבִירָה (H1377) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 11:19, with occurrences in 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גְּבִירָה (H1377) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גְּבִירָה (H1377) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גְּבִירָה (gᵉbîyrâh) / H1377 is traced through 1 Kings 11:19, 1 Kings 15:13, 2 Kings 10:13, 2 Chronicles 15:16 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him as wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.

timeline.evidenceText: Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him as wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
He also removed Maacah his mother from being queen, because she had made an abominable image for an Asherah. Asa cut down her image and burned it at the brook Kidron.
Jehu met with the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and said, “Who are you?”

Also Maacah, the mother of Asa the king, he removed from being queen, because she had made an abominable image for an Asherah; so Asa cut down her image, ground it into dust, and burned it at the brook Kidron.
Say to the king and to the queen mother,
(after Jeconiah the king, the queen mother, the eunuchs, the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the smiths, had departed from Jerusalem),

definitions.full: H1377. gebirah גְּבִירָה noun feminine 1. lady, queen , 1Kin 11:19 ; 2 queen-mother , 1Kin 15:13 2Chr 15:16 ; מִגּ ׳וַיְסִרֶהָ he removed her from (the position of) queen-mother ; compare 2Kin 10:13 ; Jer 13:18 ; 29:2 .
